latestCommentBody: The release ZIP does not contain a file literally named `setup.exe`: `scripts/build-installer.ps1:80-103` packages `WindowsCompanion-<version>-win-<arch>-setup.exe` plus its `.bin` parts. This search therefore always returns null for shipped packages, making every Install now attempt fail.

The production `_updateHttp` comes from `GitHubReleaseClient.CreateHttpClient()`, whose handler has `AllowAutoRedirect = false` (`Services/GitHubReleaseClient.cs:99-103`). GitHub `browser_download_url` asset requests redirect to the asset host, so the downloader's `EnsureSuccessStatusCode()` rejects the redirect and every real auto-download fails before verification. Use a separate asset client or explicitly validate and follow the GitHub asset redirect while retaining the no-redirect client for release API checks.

`File.WriteAllText` emits UTF-8 without a BOM, which Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads using the legacy ANSI code page. A non-ASCII user-profile or temp path is therefore corrupted in the script and the verified installer cannot be found or relaunched. Write the script with a BOM-compatible encoding.

`Progress<T>.Report` posts callbacks asynchronously. A queued final download callback can run after `Verifying` or `ReadyToInstall` has been published, and because it uses the same revision it overwrites the newer phase back to `Downloading`. Use a synchronous progress adapter or reject download-progress publications once the phase has advanced.

Asset selection happens before the current run is superseded. If a newer release has no matching assets, this branch publishes `Failed` but leaves the older download running; it can continue consuming bandwidth and leave a completed stale package even though its later publications are revision-rejected. Cancel the active run when advancing the revision for this failure path.

The presentation has no update-mode input, so it cannot implement the new mode contract: in Notify only it labels the Settings action `Install update…` instead of `View release`, and in Disabled mode the check action remains enabled even though the controller silently ignores it. Pass the current mode into the presentation and gate/label all update actions accordingly.

This only persists the mode. Automatic download is started exclusively from `OnUpdateStateChanged`, so selecting Auto-install after an update was already discovered in Notify-only mode does not download it until another check publishes state. Re-evaluate the current available update (and notify the UI) when the preference changes so the advertised immediate mode change takes effect.

The new long-running installer pipeline is subscribed here but is not included in `AppController.DisposeAsync`: shutdown cancels/awaits only `_startupUpdates` before disposing the owned update `HttpClient`. An in-flight package download or verification can therefore continue into dependency disposal and leave work/partial files behind. Unsubscribe this event and cancel/await `_updateInstaller` during controller disposal.

`StartUpdateCheck()` runs before the window is constructed (`App.xaml.cs:80-90`). This result banner is then immediately vulnerable to the automatic check's next `ApplyUpdateState`, which closes it for a Current result; on hidden startup it will be gone before the user opens the window, even though `last-install.json` was already consumed. Preserve the one-time install result until it has actually been presented or acknowledged.

The ready-state check and transition to `Installing` are not atomic. Two concurrent calls can both observe `ReadyToInstall`, then invoke the package installer twice; a new download can also advance `_revision` between the read and `Publish`, causing this install to proceed even though its state transition was rejected. Serialize installation with the same single-flight mechanism and perform the guarded state transition atomically before invoking the installer.

The helper script waits for this process to exit before starting setup, but this method only starts the helper and returns; neither controller/UI caller requests the existing graceful application shutdown. Consequently Install now reports `Installed` while the helper waits indefinitely, and installation begins only if the user later exits manually. Request `App.RequestShutdown(...)` after a successful helper handoff.

This description says installation can happen automatically, but every mode still requires the explicit Install now action. That contradicts the PR's user-consent guarantee and can mislead users about what the default mode does.

This always pins the certificate claim to `refs/tags/<tag>`, but the existing release workflow also supports `workflow_dispatch` with the tag supplied as an input while the run itself is typically on `refs/heads/main`. The attestation's Build Config URI follows the workflow-run ref, not the later checkout ref, so those legitimately published releases will always fail verification. Either require releases to run on the tag ref or validate the supported dispatch identity without weakening the repository/workflow binding.
